title: draft_field helper unwraps query errors to "", so load-bearing resumed_at == "" assertions false-pass if the raw SQL breaks
evidence:
fn draft_field(db: pog.Connection, vacancy_id: String, column: String) -> String {
  test_db.query_text(
    db,
    "SELECT COALESCE(" <> column <> "::text, '') FROM application_draft
     WHERE vacancy_id = '" <> vacancy_id <> "'::uuid",
  )
  |> result.unwrap("")
}
... and the load-bearing sites:
  draft_field(db, vacancy_id, "resumed_at") |> should.equal("")   (line 318)
  draft_field(db, other_id, "resumed_at") |> should.equal("")     (line 359)
... with test_db.query_text mapping failures to Error: `|> result.map_error(fn(_) { "Query failed" })`
detail: query_text returns Error on failure; unwrap("") turns it into "". Lines 318 (prefetch no-stamp guard) and 359 (cross-vacancy no-stamp) assert equal("") with no companion row-read guard, so a broken query (e.g. renamed column — raw SQL strings don't fail compilation) passes silently.
recommended_fix: Make draft_field panic on query error (e.g. result.lazy_unwrap/expect with message) or use a non-empty sentinel, so equal("") can only succeed from a real NULL column.

title: Exact cap boundaries unpinned: 64-char key, 120/121 entries, 4000/4001-char value never exercised
evidence:
pub fn filter_fields_caps_key_count_and_length_test() {
  let long_key = string.repeat("k", 65)
...
    int.range(1, 200, [], fn(acc, i) { [#("field_" <> pad(i), "v"), ..acc] })
...
    dict.from_list([#("personal_statement", string.repeat("x", 5000))])
... against production guards: `const max_key_length = 64` / `&& string.length(key) <= max_key_length` / `|> list.take(max_field_keys)` (120) / `#(key, string.slice(value, 0, max_value_length))` (4000)
detail: Tests pin only 65-dropped, 200→120, 5000→4000. Exactly-64 kept, 120 kept / 121 trimmed, and 4000 untouched / 4001 truncated are unpinned, so an off-by-one regression (<= to <, take(119), slice(0, 3999)) escapes detection.
recommended_fix: Add boundary cases: a 64-char key survives; exactly 120 entries all kept and 121 trimmed to 120; a 4000-char value unchanged and 4001 truncated to 4000.

title: Cooldown pinned at 9 and 11 minutes only — exactly-at-10-minutes claim behaviour untested
evidence:
stamp("9 minutes")
  let assert Ok(cooling) =
    app_sql.claim_continue_link_send(db, uuid, "tenant@example.com", "t")
  list.length(cooling.rows) |> should.equal(0)
  // 11 minutes ago → the window has passed.
  stamp("11 minutes")
... against the SQL: `OR last_link_sent_at < now() - interval '10 minutes'`
detail: The claim uses a strict `<` comparison, so a stamp exactly 10 minutes old is still on cooldown — but no test pins the boundary, so a drift to `<=` (or an off-by-one interval) would go uncaught.
recommended_fix: Optionally assert the boundary with a stamp of '10 minutes' (or '10 minutes 1 second' / '9 minutes 59 seconds') documenting the strict-< semantics.

title: resume_on_closed_vacancy test asserts only absence of resume markers — a blank or wrong 200 page passes
evidence:
resp.status |> should.equal(200)
  let body = simulate.read_body(resp)
  body
  |> string.contains("data-apply-page=\"form-resume\"")
  |> should.be_false
  body |> string.contains("draft-resume-banner") |> should.be_false
... while the closed page carries positive markers: `attribute("data-testid", "closed-vacancy-notice"),` and `html.text("Applications have closed")`
detail: Status 200 plus two negative substring checks would also pass for an empty body, an error page rendered with 200, or the wrong template. The closed-vacancy page's own testid/copy is available but never asserted.
recommended_fix: Assert a positive marker of the closed page, e.g. body contains "closed-vacancy-notice" or "Applications have closed".

title: Erasure-confirm GET with an unknown/forged token never exercised — only the valid-token confirm and the replay-POST 404 are pinned
detail: The uniform-404 contract is pinned for resume (resume_with_unknown_token_is_uniform_404_test) and for the erasure POST replay, but the erasure-confirm GET's bad-token path — the link a mail-scanner or attacker actually probes — has no test.
recommended_fix: Add a GET draft-erasure test with an unknown token asserting 404 and the draft-not-found marker, mirroring resume_with_unknown_token_is_uniform_404_test.
